title: Testing Reducers
description: Learn how to write comprehensive unit tests for Redux reducers using Jest and React Testing Library.

data.text: Testing is crucial for maintaining reliable Redux applications. Reducers are particularly easy to test because they are **pure functions**. Given the same input state and action, a reducer always returns the same output. No mocking, no async complexity, just straightforward input-output verification.
This lesson covers how to write comprehensive reducer tests that verify your state management logic works correctly for all possible cases.

Reducers contain your application's core logic for state transitions. Testing them thoroughly gives you confidence that your state changes work correctly, regardless of what components or side effects interact with them.

cards.title: Unit Tests (Reducers)
cards.content:
Test state logic in isolation
No rendering or DOM needed
Fast execution
Easy to pinpoint failures
Test edge cases thoroughly

cards.title: Integration Tests
cards.content:
Test full user flows
Includes components and store
Slower to run
Tests real user behavior
Catches integration bugs

data.text: A good reducer test suite covers: the initial state, each action type, edge cases, and invalid action handling. Each test should be focused and readable.

data.title: Reducer Test Structure

data.text: Many actions carry payload data. Your tests should verify that the reducer correctly uses this payload to update state.

data.title: Testing Payload Actions

data.text: Reducers using entity adapters have consistent patterns. You can test the adapter operations directly without worrying about implementation details.

data.title: Testing Entity Adapter Reducers
Reducer Test Checklist
items: Test initial state when state is undefined
Test each action type with typical input
Test each action type with edge cases (empty, zero, max values)
Test that original state is not mutated
Test that extra state fields are preserved
Use descriptive test names that explain what is being tested

terms.definition: A function that always returns the same output for the same input and has no side effects.
A test that verifies a single unit of code in isolation.
A pure function that takes the current state and an action, returning the next state.
Checking that all nested properties of objects are equal, not just the reference.
Not modifying the original state, but returning a new state object.

data.title: Write Reducer Tests
data.description: Write comprehensive tests for a shopping cart slice with add, remove, update quantity, and clear operations.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Reducers are pure functions and easy to test
Test initial state first with undefined input
Cover each action type with typical and edge cases
Use descriptive test names that explain the scenario
Verify immutability by checking original state is unchanged
Group related tests with describe blocks for organization
data.takeaway: Reducer tests are fast, reliable, and give you confidence in your state management logic.
